examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
examples.problem: Find $\angle BAC$ given the points $A(2,-1,-5)$, $B(-1,0,-4)$, and $C(5,1,1).$ Round your answer to $1$ decimal place.
examples.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A$, $B$, $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨2,-1,-5⟩,\,b=⟨-1,0,-4⟩,\,c=⟨5,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $\triangle ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $\angle BAC = \theta.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13964292/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨-1,0,-4⟩-⟨2,-1,-5⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,1,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨5,1,1⟩-⟨2,-1,-5⟩ \\  & =⟨3,2,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{-3\cdot 3+1\cdot 2+1\cdot 6}{\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-1}{\sqrt{11}\sqrt{49}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{7\sqrt{11}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta = \arccos \left( -\dfrac{1}{7\sqrt{11}} \right) \approx 92.5^\circ.
$$

feedback.problem: Find the angle between $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
Rearranging the dot product formula, we have: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot (-1)+3\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{3}^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{11}{\sqrt{14}\cdot \sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{11}{3\sqrt{14}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{11}{3\sqrt{14}})≈{11.49}^{∘}.
$$
